title: Fantastic Content, Terrible Navigation
text:
Hi, I love the content in this app. The meditations, the courses, the move workouts, the sleepcasts/music, it’s all great. Since the content is what’s most important, my rating is high. The content alone would be equivalent to a 5 star rating.

That being said, the app is SUCH a pain to navigate. I have to remember how to get to pages myself, because the “recommended for you” content on the front page is never related to what I’ve actually been doing in your app. 

There’s also no option to add in details of your life that might prevent you from receiving certain reccommended content. For example; I have no kids, and there are many meditations, ones that keep getting recommended to me, about being a parent. I should be able to mark an option to hide all of this content, or at the very least, tell the app to stop giving me it as a recommendation.

So in conclusion; content is fantastic. Actually got me to stick with a meditation and move schedule, and absolutely love it. PLEASE make the app itself work better on a functional level. I shouldn’t have to search “Walking” every day when I want to find a walking meditation.

Also give me an option to turn Ebb off. They aren’t helpful, and cause me more annoyance than anything because it literally cannot answer any question I ask it, and it simply just gives me the same 3 basic meditations as an answer every time.

title: Professionals deem AI as unethical for therapy

But the more egregious error is this Ebb thing. I have not used it because I have social workers in my family and they all agree AI is unethical. Headspace should not be pushing this. Fortunately there is a feature to meet with real therapists, much better
But overall this app has all the signs of a group that no longer cares and just has a collection of good meditation IP.

title: App is great, the experience not so much
text:
If I’m just reviewing the app, it’s fine; the app works well, is easy enough to navigate, video is good. 

That said, the overall Talkspace experience is pretty terrible - the therapists are fairly subpar, there isn’t a big selection of them (I tried to change and kept getting offered the same ones), and their policies are super inflexible. e.g., my son broke his arm and I had to take him to the hospital. I messaged my therapist that I had to miss our session, and her only (and repeated) response was that I was going to be charged $140 for missing our session, and there was nothing she could do.  

Anyway, my recommendation is to avoid Talkspace and just look to other platforms, or reach out to some local therapists; they will likely have video capabilities themselves.

Overall I love the app, how easy it is to change a provider when I feel they aren’t a good match, as well as the fact that despite not every provider being a good match, they have ALL given me some big take away to work with.

title: DON’T TRUST THE FAKE REVIEWS!
text:
Talkspace is failing both administratively and clinically.  They also have a very high number of complaints on BBB. For a platform intended to create a safe space and help you feel secure, it does the exact opposite.

1. Administrative Negligence & Broken Protocols-

The support system is fundamentally broken. I have followed up through every possible channel, yet the platform fails to follow its own administrative protocols:

• The Ticket Void: I have submitted multiple tickets regarding technical issues and provider care. They do not respond consistently or quickly enough to resolve anything, leaving tickets open for weeks. Even when the Clinical Quality Team promises a 3-day response for serious complaints, they regularly blow past their own deadlines with no real updates even after I have followed up multiple times.

• Unreachable Phone Support: I tried calling their support line twice in the morning—specifically to avoid a queue—an hour apart. Both times, I was kept on hold for exactly 12 minutes before an automated voice claimed they were "closed" and hung up on me during their stated business hours.

• Agonizingly Slow Chat: Live chat agents take 5 minutes to respond to every single message, turning basic questions into painfully long ordeals that result in no resolution. All they do is direct you back to creating a ticket. If you’ve already done so, they then promise that you’ll get a response within three days, which you won’t. 


2. Lack of Transparency-

Talkspace provides no patient reviews for their therapists, forcing you into a "trial and error" loop. If their providers are to be trusted, they should be transparent with patient feedback so users can find a proper fit without constant provider changes.


3. Failure of Clinical Neutrality-

My spouse and I entered our first joint session in total agreement on our goals since we are separated. This is a rare and positive alignment for a separated couple. Yet, rather than celebrating our common goals, the therapist completely abandoned clinical neutrality to push her own narrative.

She criticized our intentions from the very start and claimed meeting as a family unit with our children would "confuse" them, ignoring our consensus that this was for their benefit. I had to politely ask her three times to stop questioning our intentions and redirect her back to our goals before she finally complied. It was an unprofessional attempt to create conflict and dysfunction where none existed.


Final Note to Talkspace: 

I have already reached out via email and followed up through every possible channel regarding these issues, so do not respond with a generic request for me to contact you again.

I honestly don’t expect anything to come out of this review or my open tickets because you have continuously made empty promises to resolve these issues. This lack of timely action is only creating more problems for me personally. Ultimately, this platform is marketed as a way to help you feel heard and safe, yet it fails to achieve that even within its own internal processes. You are not providing a safe space when your support is unreachable and your clinical oversight is terrible or non-existent.

title: Predatory App
text:
This app has nothing to do with therapy and everything to do with manipulation. I had an extremely misogynistic “therapist” who told me to stop talking to my husband about “issues” as he simply can’t understand “issues”. My husbands “therapist” asked him a deep question, waited for him to answer, then said “well time for my next session bye!” And just ended the session right there. Piss poor therapeutic models. No ability to follow through or connect to other professionals. No discharge planning. Preying on the weak and those asking for help. Genuinely horrible app. 

Their pricing model is also ludicrous as well as the fact they are set up to just bill you and say “oh by the way we took half your rent payment! Hope therapy worked 😌”. It didn’t. Your providers are awful. 

As a social worker I’m appalled and will be taking the appropriate actions to report every person we have dealt with to our state licensing boards, if they are even licensed. I can’t fathom any mental health professional worth their weight wanting to put their name behind this app. Disgusting.

title: Dione deserves ten stars!
text:
Hi,
I am spending time to write this review expecting that Dione will get the credit, acknowledgement and praise that she absolutely deserves. 

Had I not used Included Health during the 2024-2025 years, I would have completely lost my mind and gone bananas on some of these insurance companies. My involvement with Dione started in early 2024, when I started getting bills for the birth of my third child. I gave birth 2 weeks before the end of the year, our insurance changed and then my sweet son was put into the NICU (into the 2024 year). I would have never expected the nightmare of bills, miscommunication, runarounds, people not documenting well etc that occurred. It took Dione over a year to get all the bills settled (when I had great insurance all along). I could not have survived without her. 

Fast forward 6 months after my son was born, my other son began having unexplainable grand mal seizures. He was 3 at the time they started happening and again, Dione came to our rescue. MRIs not covered, EEGs that should have been covered for 24-hours but we were constantly billed or double billed. A completely nightmare in the midst of dealing with a newborn and the fear of my other son losing his life to these episodes. 

In a year and a half of feeling unheard and unseen by so many professionals, Dione always redeemed me. She followed up in a timely manner. Kept track of all the bills, their status and what was happening with them. She advocated hard for us and it was more than appreciated. 

Then, my mother died unexpectedly while visiting us. You know when your patience for greedy humans runs out and you wish life wasn’t so complicated? I was there. I was done. Dione wasn’t. She STILL showed up for us to offer compassions and support in an awful time. She took the battles off my plate over and over and over again. The weight of that cannot be put into enough words of gratitude. I’m sure she had so many days she too wanted to ring the necks of people not doing their jobs or not caring about their jobs, but she always handled our case with such grace. She was the light in our very dark tunnel. Her voice was positive and her words always validating. 

For the same person to help us through three very big turning points in our life is unheard of. She doesn’t know us. She could have easily dismissed us, made me feel like my complaints and frustrations were only my own… but she didn’t. She made us feel like she was on our side, doing the right thing and always available to help. 

It’s very hard to find such dedicated employees like her. Extremely hard to find people like her who still find joy and grace in a job that naturally has its frustrations. I applaud Dione to the utmost level and truly could not have survived the last year and a half without her. Whatever had to happen to keep her on my case, THANK YOU. She was phenomenal and someone who represents your organization and department so well. I will forever talk about Included Health to others BECAUSE OF HER. I hope she is given the acknowledgement she deserves. And if ever she wants to leave, I would highly suggest going above and beyond to never lose her. She is a huge asset to your team. 

With great gratitude,
Sarina Barker

title: Terrible Provider
text: I booked an appointment with Dr. Madeline Jacobs [C], MD for a consult to manage medication and establish care. The appointment was for 12:45pm and I was on time. When I signed in for my appointment the app was not recognizing that my camera was on. I let the provider know it wasn’t working and that I would have to switch devices. You could hear the attitude in her voice as she told me that she couldn’t help me if she couldn’t see me on camera; all while she wasn’t even in the camera frame. I could only see the side of her hair. I told her I understood and that’s why I was getting a different device. When I was able to login on a different device it was 12:48pm and she proceeded to tell me with the tone of a scolding mother that I had to hurry up because I had already wasted so much of her time. I reminded her the appointment was for 12:45pm and it had only been 3 minutes since the original start time. She began to reply something in a condescending tone so I cut her off. I thanked her for her time and told her I’d be ending the appointment because I didn’t appreciate her attitude or the tone of her voice. She rolled her eyes at me and said okay. She didn’t even take the time to make a proper introduction. Accessing physical and mental care via telehealth is already awkward enough as it is. There is no need to have an attitude when it was a minor delay caused by something not in my control.

title: A Safe Space to Heal & Grow
text: BetterHelp has made it easier for me to take the first steps toward prioritizing my mental health and working through things I’ve been carrying for a long time. As a mom trying to navigate recovery, family struggles, custody, and rebuilding my life, having a space where I can talk openly and work on myself means a lot. I appreciate having the opportunity to connect with a therapist and focus on becoming a healthier, stronger version of myself. Healing isn’t always easy, but taking that first step feels good.

title: Won’t let you put in insurance
text: Tried three different times and with different emails and responses and I answered my income was ok and it refused to let me put in insurance info only would want me to charge it. Clearly won’t pay when my insurance is only 25 and my husband somehow for that but he stated he was a student for which he is but I’m not. I’m employed. Clearly they want a ploy to force people to pay up front because it won’t let me apply my insurance card and did EXACTLY how my husband did minus student and income. Not worth my time, caused more stress to try and get a therapist through it. Would need a therapy session after going through the entrance frustration.

title: Therapy for me
text:
I love my therapist. She’s always available, she’s the best listener and honestly one of my best friends now. I am glad I joined, even though my husband had to convince me to. 
It was definitely worth it. 
I’m not great at self care, meditation or mindfulness. 
I’m a woman going through the throws of menopause, panic attacks and loss of self love. 
Plus we have an adult special needs kid who takes up 100% of our days, both with full time jobs. Therapy just sounded like another job I would need to clock in for. 
But this is a wonderful experience for me to barf up all my feelings freely. It is a real release. 
At least my hub doesn’t have to take it all. 🤮🤷🏼‍♀️😳😬😂

title: Excellent mental health treatment
text: I heard of BetterHelp through one of my favorite books, Depression is a Liar, in Danny Baker mentioning it and all the advertisement all over my social networking. I decided to give it all a try, and so far it's going great! As I have suffered three brain aneurysms, three brain bleeds, a stroke, mood disorder, and major depressive disorder, a headache disorder, and a diagnosis my medical team and I are unsure how to diagnose quite yet, this platform has been great!

title: DON’T WASTE YOUR TIME
text: They currently have an active lawsuit against them for leaking private patient data! Before I learned this, I couldn’t even get an appointment because they don’t take my insurance or my husband’s. Without insurance, it’s not affordable.

title: Virtual Therapy
text: My husband was diagnosed with cancer and I became his main caregiver and I was happy to do so. However the diagnosis also rocked my whole world and there were many emotions I was dealing with and my daughter suggested Better Help as she had used them to help her through a difficult time. I decided to give it a try as being the main caregiver did not allow me time to visit a therapist in person and be away from my husband as his situation was fluid. I was able to find a therapist who had been through many of the things I was going through and seeing her once a week has helped me so much. If you are in need of a therapist and seeing one in person is either not possible or not something you want to do I strongly suggest you try Better Help. It is also much less expensive than seeing a therapist in person and with an I Pad or phone you are still talking face to face. They also have an option of just an audio visit if you prefer.

title: Quick and easy!
text: My son in law tried better help and liked it.  I found that I needed some help myself and gave BetterHelp a shot.  It was fast and easy to navigate!  I just had my first session and it was great!🙏🏼❤️🙏🏼

title: Get started here
text: Not knowing anything about counseling, besides what I’ve heard from my wife and daughters, I was intimidated. This app makes it easy to get help quickly. Definitely recommend.

title: This has been life saving
text:
I have been seeing a wonderful therapist from BetterHelp for the past year & it has been a wonderful experience. I have been in 2 severe vehicle accidents 11 months apart. I then lost my 51 yr old son in February 2025 & I just lost my husband in June 2026 after a very brief illness from brain cancer. 

I am grateful I’ve had BetterHelp to get me through these tough times. My therapist, Anna, is professional yet caring & is very knowledgeable & experienced. I get to schedule my own appointments according to my schedule, am able to message my therapist at any time & use the journaling & other tools available to keep me moving forward.

title: Doesn’t take insurance
text: This app seemed to have many great qualities except for the affordability and the lack of insurance taking. I’m a single mother of a 1 year old baby girl and college student. Even with the financial aid this app provides, I cannot afford $205+ a month to get the help that I need. Very unfortunate.

title: Realization made for good
text: This app came at a time when I really needed it. I think God showed me this app to help me.  I’ve been struggling with my marriage, taking care of elderly mother, grieving the loss of my father, and aging . I was at a breaking point when my mother died. I found this app to be very helpful and the counselor I am teamed up with is a great resource and I have felt very comfortable talking and discussing what the issues are. If you need help, this app is very worth it. My insurance covers the visits and I can schedule appointments easily and as often as I need them. You still have to work on yourself but having this guidance is helpful. I would recommend BetterHelp app for everyone.
